record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: Let t ≥ 3, and let F be a family of graphs on vertex set [n] such that for every G, H in F, the intersection G ∩ H has chromatic number at least t. Must |F| be at most 2^{(n choose 2) - (t choose 2)}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3. Let t ≥ 3. If F is a family of graphs on the vertex-set [n] such that for all G, H ∈ F, G ∩ H has chromatic number at least t, then |F| ≤ 2^((n choose 2)−(t choose 2)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $t \geq 3$ be an integer and let $n \geq 1$. Consider graphs on the labeled vertex set $[n] = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, identified with their edge sets (so there are $2^{\binom{n}{2}}$ such graphs). For two graphs $G$ and $H$ on $[n]$, let $G \cap H$ denote the graph on $[n]$ whose edge set is the intersection of the edge sets of $G$ and $H$, and let $\chi(\cdot)$ denote chromatic number.

A family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs on $[n]$ is called \emph{$t$-chromatic-intersecting} if for every $G, H \in \mathcal{F}$ (including $G = H$) one has $\chi(G \cap H) \geq t$.

Prove or disprove: for every $t \geq 3$ and every $n$, every $t$-chromatic-intersecting family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs on $[n]$ satisfies
$$|\mathcal{F}| \leq 2^{\binom{n}{2} - \binom{t}{2}}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous (weaker) $K_t$-intersecting conjecture, which would be implied by the chromatic version, has been proved only for $t=3$ (Ellis–Filmus–Friedgut, 2012) and $t=4$ (Berger–Zhao); it remains open for $t \geq 5$. The stronger chromatic-intersecting formulation appears to be open in general, with only partial results (e.g. weaker bounds of the form $2^{\binom{n}{2}-(\chi(H)-1)}$ for $H$-intersecting families).

status_evidence.title: On H-Intersecting Graph Families
status_evidence.snippet: For K_t-intersecting families: t=3 proved by Ellis, Filmus & Friedgut (2012); t=4 proved by Berger and Zhao; t≥5 open.
status_evidence.claim: The K_t-intersecting case (implied by chromatic-intersecting) is only known for t=3,4 and open for t≥5.

status_evidence.title: K4-intersecting families of graphs (Berger and Zhao)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the K_4-intersecting case of the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The K_4-intersecting case was proved by Berger and Zhao.
